Subject: Science
Chapters: Chemical Reactions & Equations; Acids, Bases & Salts; Metals & Non-metals; Carbon & its Compounds
How to write the answer: Write balanced equations with state symbols and name the type of reaction. For carbon compounds, draw the structure and give the IUPAC name.
How to prepare fast: Make one page of every reaction in the four chapters and read it daily. Practise pH, uses of salts and the reactivity series from past papers.

Subject: Science
Chapters: Life Processes; Control & Coordination; How do Organisms Reproduce?; Heredity
How to write the answer: Draw and label the diagrams — heart, nephron, neuron, flower, alimentary canal. Use NCERT keywords and answer in points.
How to prepare fast: Practise the eight to ten standard diagrams until each takes two minutes. For Heredity, practise Mendel's monohybrid and dihybrid crosses.

Subject: Science
Chapters: Electricity; Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
How to write the answer: For numericals write the formula, then the values with units, then the answer with its unit. Draw circuits with the correct symbols.
How to prepare fast: Learn Ohm's law, resistances in series and parallel, and the power and heating formulas, then solve 15–20 numericals from past papers.

Subject: Science
Chapters: Light – Reflection & Refraction; The Human Eye & the Colourful World
How to write the answer: Draw ray diagrams with a ruler and arrows. Use the sign convention in mirror and lens numericals and show every step.
How to prepare fast: Practise the six mirror and six lens ray-diagram cases and the mirror and lens formulas. Revise defects of vision and how they are corrected.

Subject: Science
How to write the answer: Short answers with an example: a food chain, the 10% law, the ozone layer.
How to prepare fast: A short chapter: read the NCERT text once and revise the in-text questions for quick marks.

Subject: Mathematics
Chapters: Polynomials; Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables; Quadratic Equations; Arithmetic Progressions
How to write the answer: Write the formula first, then every step, and box the final answer. CBSE gives marks for steps even when the final answer is wrong.
How to prepare fast: The biggest unit. Do the NCERT examples and exercises, then word problems on quadratic equations and APs from the last two years' papers.

Subject: Mathematics
How to write the answer: Write Given, To Prove, Construction and Proof, with a reason for every step, and draw a neat figure.
How to prepare fast: Learn the proofs of the Basic Proportionality Theorem and the tangent theorems — they are asked often. Then practise similarity problems.

Subject: Mathematics
Chapters: Introduction to Trigonometry; Some Applications of Trigonometry
How to write the answer: For heights and distances always draw the figure and mark the angles. For identities, work on one side only.
How to prepare fast: Memorise the ratio table and the three identities, then practise ten identity proofs and ten heights-and-distances problems.

Subject: Mathematics
How to write the answer: Build the full table (class mark, frequency, cumulative frequency) before using the formula. For probability, write the total outcomes first.
How to prepare fast: Very scoring: practise mean, median and mode of grouped data, and dice, card and coin probability.

Subject: Mathematics
Chapters: Areas Related to Circles; Surface Areas & Volumes
How to write the answer: Write the formula, substitute, and keep the units (cm², cm³). Draw the combined solid.
How to prepare fast: Make a formula sheet and practise questions on combinations of solids.

Subject: Mathematics
How to write the answer: Show the prime factorisation clearly. Write irrationality proofs by contradiction.
How to prepare fast: Quick marks: HCF and LCM, and the proofs that √2 and √3 are irrational.

Subject: Mathematics
How to write the answer: Write the distance or section formula, then substitute.
How to prepare fast: Only two formulas to learn — distance and section — so these are easy marks.

Subject: Social Science
Chapters: India and the Contemporary World – II (5 chapters) and map work
How to write the answer: Answer in points with dates and names. For 5-mark answers write an opening line, four or five points and a closing line. Practise the history map items.
How to prepare fast: Start with Nationalism in India and The Rise of Nationalism in Europe, the longest chapters, and make a timeline of events.

Subject: Social Science
Chapters: Contemporary India – II (7 chapters) and map work
How to write the answer: Give examples — crops, states, industries. On the map, mark accurately and label clearly.
How to prepare fast: Practise the official map list for five minutes every day, and learn crops, minerals and industries as tables.

Subject: Social Science
How to write the answer: Define the term, then explain it with examples, such as Belgium and Sri Lanka for power sharing.
How to prepare fast: A short book for 20 marks. Read each chapter twice and make one page of notes per chapter.

Subject: Social Science
How to write the answer: Define terms exactly — GDP, sectors, credit — and use the tables and data from the NCERT book.
How to prepare fast: Practise the case-based questions in the sample paper; they are built on data tables.

Subject: English (Language & Literature)
Chapters: First Flight; Footprints without Feet; grammar; letter and analytical paragraph
How to write the answer: Keep to the word limit and follow the format exactly (a letter needs address, date, subject and salutation). In literature answers, refer to characters and events by name.
How to prepare fast: Read a summary of every chapter, practise two formal letters and two analytical paragraphs, and solve the unseen passages in past papers.

Subject: Hindi (Course A / B)
Chapters: Kshitij and Kritika (A); Sparsh and Sanchayan (B); grammar; letter and notice
How to write the answer: Answer in clear points, follow the letter and notice formats, and give one example for each grammar rule.
How to prepare fast: Learn each poet's and author's name with the main idea of the piece. Grammar is the quickest source of marks, so practise it from past papers.
